A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CREMA and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. All 25 pages, including equations, Tables 1–22 and Figures 1–5, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original CREMA fine-tuning and zero-shot experiments in Section 4, with additional benchmark results, ablations and qualitative analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains the original CREMA experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including benchmark evaluations and component ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain identical multimodal Q-Former adapters, self-gated fusion, modality-sequential training and adaptive early exit. The inference procedures are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MUSIC-AVQA, SQA3D, NExT-QA, TouchQA, ThermalQA, VGGSound and PerceptionTest with the same modality coverage. Appendix A retains the same pretraining data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including BLIP-2, 3D-LLM, OneLLM, X-InstructBLIP and task-specific baselines in Tables 1–6 and 13–14.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same splits, metrics, preprocessing, model configurations and evaluation procedures. Training budgets, frame counts and prompts in Tables 10–12 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The early-exit, fusion and easy/hard-question analyses remain identical. Appendix B retains the same training, pretraining, LoRA-rank, modality-prioritization, projection and query-length ablations, alongside unchanged qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical throughout the main text and appendices. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing information is added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, CREMA retains 54.6 average accuracy on SQA3D with V,P,D,N in Table 2 and 73.9 on NExT-QA with V,F,D,N in Table 3. Appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(3) and early-exit criterion are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about modality extensibility, efficient fusion and training, and better or comparable reasoning performance with substantially fewer trainable parameters.

C2.justification: Result interpretations in Section 4.3 and Appendix B are identical. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning temporal modeling, modality-extraction overhead and potentially biased or inappropriate outputs.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and pretraining instructions remain unchanged. The project link, code/model availability statements and Appendix D licensing information also match.

R1.justification: The reference list and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 2's discussion of prior multimodal approaches and CREMA's relationship to them.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the preprint header with an ICLR 2025 publication header and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Page 11 adds thanks to reviewers and an NIH funding acknowledgement. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The running header and first-page stamp change, author spacing shifts slightly, and the expanded acknowledgement causes local reference-spacing changes on page 11. All figures and tables retain their design, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 updates publication metadata and acknowledgements, including NIH support, with minor layout adjustments. The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain identical throughout both PDFs and their appendices. These administrative changes do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or decline.
